post.description: Like POST /turns, but releases the reply sentence by sentence as it is generated.

200.description: Newline-delimited JSON events: {type: pace, slow} (whether the turn waits for the language model), {type: sentence, text} for each released sentence, then {type: done, session} or {type: error, status, detail}.

post.description: Transcribe one 16 kHz mono WAV recording. The audio is not stored.

Synthesise a sentence the character has said, or one of the case's authored
hesitations, in the given voice. Not stored.
Record that the candidate spoke over the character (hands-free conversation).

Response Drafts Api Authoring Drafts Get

AffectChange.title: AffectChange
AffectChange.description: A change in the character's affect stage; question 0 is the start of the interview.

AffectStage.title: AffectStage
AffectStage.description:
How the character feels at one point in the interview.

The first stage applies from the start. A stage with rapport_at_least applies once the
running rapport reaches that level; an on_confrontation stage applies for the turn of a
confrontational line and the turn after, and takes precedence.

expression and hesitations are presentation only: how the 3D character looks, and
fillers it may voice while thinking. Neither changes what it knows or reveals.

AuthoringOptions.title: AuthoringOptions
AuthoringOptions.description: Permitted values, published from the Python schema so the editor cannot drift.

CaseSummary.title: CaseSummary
CaseSummary.description: What a candidate may see before and during a station; never the hidden facts.

CharacterQuestion.title: CharacterQuestion
CharacterQuestion.description:
A question the character asks, appended verbatim to its reply once due.

after_fact: on the turn that fact is first revealed (or the next free turn after).
after_seconds: on the first turn this far into the interview. Authors must make sure
a question reveals nothing the candidate has not yet elicited.

Fact.title: Fact
Fact.description:
Something the role-player knows, and when it may be revealed.

volunteered: may be offered unprompted. on_direct_question: only once the
candidate asks about one of ``asked_about``. after_rapport: as for a direct
question, but only after the candidate has shown empathy or acknowledgement.
``asked_about`` labels are what the interpreter matches questions against, so even
volunteered facts need them; keep labels distinctive between facts.

note.title: Note
note.default: Automated feedback for practice. It shows which case information your questions elicited and describes how you asked; it is not a CASC mark, the case has not been clinically validated, and the indicators can be wrong.

Presentation.title: Presentation
Presentation.description:
How the 3D character currently looks: the affect stage's expression and the fillers it
may voice while thinking. Says nothing about facts or disclosure.

label.title: Label
label.default: Rule preview: question recognition and generated replies are not tested.

note.title: Note
note.default: Time-based character questions are not simulated. Rapport decays each turn, adds the line's empathy (0–2) and loses 1 for a confrontational line.

Readiness.title: Readiness
Readiness.description:
Text role-play needs valid cases and registry; local mode also needs generation.

Speech is optional: typed input works whether or not speech recognition is ready, and
replies can be read in a browser voice when the character's voice is not.

SpeechView.title: SpeechView
SpeechView.description: Audio (base64 WAV) with word and viseme timings in ms from the start of the audio.

Task.title: Task
Task.description:
A candidate action. Feedback marks it met from a linked communication indicator or
an elicited fact; tasks with neither are left for the candidate's self-review.

VoiceHint.title: VoiceHint
VoiceHint.description: How the character should sound when replies are read aloud; not a hidden fact.
